advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intentional relocation of the selector into a single fixture_selection.py and the corpus test into tests/unit/ vs the ticket's declared fixture_mining/ modules and tests/integration/ path.
evidence: test_fixture_selection_corpus.py docstring: 'Runs under tests/unit/** where the repository's network-escape guard is active.'
advisory.finding: The change's structure diverges from the ticket's declared file_impact without explanation: the ticket lists src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_mining/select.py + manifest.py and tests/integration/test_fixture_selection_corpus.py, but the implementation ships a single src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py and places the corpus determinism test under tests/unit/ (renamed to test_fixture_selection_corpus.py). The AC9 real-corpus determinism test therefore runs under the unit network guard rather than as an integration test as scoped.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the time-unit contract of last_rubric_commit_ts (seconds) with review_event_ts (nanoseconds) so the default select_candidates path applies the vintage gate correctly rather than relying on select_from_corpus's ns wrapper.
evidence: fixture_selection.py:136 `[r for r in reviews if int(r["review_event_ts"]) > rubric_ts]`
fixture_selection.py:427-431 `_rubric_history_ns` returns `seconds * 1_000_000_000` — a ns conversion needed precisely because corpus review_event_ts is ns
corpus.py:87 `_Blob(sha, m["tid"], int(m["ts"]), ...)` with ts parsed from the nanosecond-epoch event filename; labels.py:120 documents 'raw nanosecond-epoch comparison'
blocking.finding: The default vintage-gate path mixes time units: last_rubric_commit_ts returns EPOCH SECONDS (git '--format=%ct'), but corpus review_event_ts is EPOCH NANOSECONDS. When select_candidates is called with rubric_history=None (its documented default), _eligible_reviews compares review_event_ts (ns) > rubric_ts (s), so every real review trivially clears the gate. The bug is masked only because select_from_corpus injects a _rubric_history_ns wrapper that multiplies seconds by 1_000_000_000; any direct caller of select_candidates over corpus rows gets a silently-disabled vintage gate.
blocking.suggested_fix: Normalize both sides to one unit in _eligible_reviews (e.g. have last_rubric_commit_ts return ns, or scale review_event_ts down), and drop the ad-hoc *1e9 in select_from_corpus.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Populate ticket_state in select_from_corpus (e.g. via labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override) so the escaped_defect priority signal actually fires on the real corpus, or document that it is intentionally deferred.
evidence: fixture_selection.py:423 `review["ticket_state"] = review.get("ticket_state", {})` — corpus rows have no ticket_state key, so this is always {}
corpus.py:270-288 `_build_sidecar_row` return dict has no `ticket_state` field
labels.py:282 `_read_ticket_state_via_env_override` exists to read real ticket state but is not used here
blocking.finding: In select_from_corpus the escaped_defect priority signal can never fire: corpus rows from build_corpus/_build_sidecar_row carry no ticket_state, and the enrichment loop sets `review["ticket_state"] = review.get("ticket_state", {})` which is always the empty dict. labels.escaped_defect({}) is always False, so the escaped-defect rank boost (ticket AC7) is inert on the real corpus even though labels.py provides _read_ticket_state_via_env_override to actually read it. The unit tests only cover this via synthetic ticket_state injection, so the gap is invisible.
